page: Microsoft Azure FX16-4ms_v2 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the FXmsv2 family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The physical hardware consists of 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. This configuration is paired with an exceptionally high memory allocation of 336.0 GB of RAM, translating to 84.0 GB of memory per physical core. The CPU includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for tile and integer operations. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile characterized by strong single-core execution and constrained multi-core scaling. The server achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core and text processing tests, alongside strong single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core performance is weak, as evidenced by stress-ng multi-core and multi-threaded decompression scores. Memory bandwidth also shows a significant drop-off, measuring average speeds for cached small blocks but falling to weak rates for uncached large blocks.

Given the massive memory-to-vCPU ratio of 84 GB per core, this server offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU scaling. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for applications requiring large in-memory datasets but minimal compute overhead, avoiding the need to provision higher vCPU counts just to secure sufficient RAM. Appropriate workloads include memory-intensive database operations, caching layers like Redis, and text processing tasks. It is less suitable for heavily parallelized compute tasks, software compilation, or large-scale LLM inference.
